verdicts.quote: “The API uses Bearer token authentication. Include your API key in the Authorization header of every request: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY.”
verdicts.reason: Vendor API reference explicitly shows API-key-as-Bearer header for all requests, which fits “Bearer/PAT token.” ([transcriptapi.com](https://transcriptapi.com/docs/api/))

verdicts.quote: “New users receive 100 free credits upon registration. These credits expire 90 days after account creation and are non-refundable.”
verdicts.reason: Credentials are self-serve, but the free access is explicitly time-limited credits (90‑day expiry), which matches “self_serve_trial,” not an ongoing “self_serve_free” tier. ([transcriptapi.com](https://transcriptapi.com/terms))

verdicts.quote: Endpoint list includes: “GET /youtube/transcript … GET /youtube/info … GET /youtube/video/metadata … GET /youtube/search … GET /youtube/channel/resolve … GET /youtube/channel/info … GET /youtube/channel/search … GET /youtube/channel/videos … GET /youtube/channel/playlists … GET /youtube/channel/posts … GET /youtube/channel/sections … GET /youtube/channel/latest … GET /youtube/playlist/videos.”
verdicts.reason: The API covers transcripts plus search, channel, playlist, and metadata surfaces across a dozen read endpoints—more than “narrow,” but not “dozens+ resources/full CRUD,” so “moderate” fits. ([transcriptapi.com](https://transcriptapi.com/docs/api/))

verdicts.quote: “TranscriptAPI runs a hosted (remote) MCP server at ‘https://transcriptapi.com/mcp’… There is nothing to install or host.”
verdicts.reason: This is the vendor’s own site stating they host the MCP server; that’s an official MCP. ([transcriptapi.com](https://transcriptapi.com/docs/mcp/?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “Rate limits depend on your plan: … Starter Monthly | 200 requests per minute … Starter Annual … | 300 requests per minute.”
verdicts.reason: It’s buildable now with self-serve creds and docs, but plan‑based rate limits (and the paid plan after trial) are material constraints, so “ready_with_caveats” is more accurate than “ready.” ([transcriptapi.com](https://transcriptapi.com/docs/api/))
